title: Decoding neutrophil spatial heterogeneity and clinical implications in breast cancer
abstract: Neutrophils are heterogeneous and critical components of the tumor microenvironment, yet their spatial heterogeneity and clinical implications remain poorly understood. We establish large-scale breast cancer cohorts integrating AI-powered computational pathology (n = 1,113) and single-cell spatial omics (n = 104) to investigate the clinical relevance and biological mechanisms underlying neutrophil spatial patterns. Clinical implications were greatest in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC): neutrophil-tumor cell proximity associated with favorable prognosis, while neutrophil-immune cell proximity predicted superior immunotherapy response. Combining these patterns with established biomarkers improved TNBC stratification for prognosis and immunotherapy efficacy. Spatial omics and experimental validation demonstrated that tumor-proximal neutrophils enhanced MHC I expression on tumor cells via inflammatory crosstalk, promoting immune-mediated tumor clearance and improved prognosis. Neutrophils adjacent to immune cells exhibited an antigen-presenting phenotype, augmentable by targeting polyamine metabolism. Our study highlights the functional diversity and spatial heterogeneity of neutrophils and provides a translational strategy with routine computational pathology.

title: A stroma-sensing TGF-β blockade reprograms CAF-myeloid niches to induce durable tumor immunity
abstract: Transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) accumulation in the tumor microenvironment (TME) is a major barrier to durable antitumor immunity. We developed fibronectin extra domain B (FN-EDB)-binding peptide (FEBP)-soluble TβRII-Fc (sTβRII), an engineered inhibitor targeting the FN-EDB-rich tumor matrix for localized TGF-β blockade. In fibrotic, immune-excluded tumors, FEBP-sTβRII suppresses TGF-β/SMAD signaling to unleash T cell activation and IFN-γ production, thereby driving feedforward cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-myeloid reprogramming toward an antigen-presenting state. This coordinated remodeling relieves immune exclusion and converts the fibrotic TME into an antigen-visible ecosystem that sustains robust T cell infiltration and activation. Consequently, FEBP-sTβRII induces T cell-dependent tumor regression, expands effector-memory populations, and elicits long-term, cross-protective antitumor immunity, while minimizing peripheral transcriptional disturbances compared with systemic sTβRII. Together, these findings show that spatially targeted TGF-β blockade overcomes fibrotic immune exclusion to establish durable local and systemic tumor immunity.

title: Neutrophils are known by their neighbors in breast cancer
abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Xu et al. combine large-scale computational pathology, spatial omics, and functional experiments to examine neutrophil organization in triple-negative breast tumors. They identify two neutrophil niches with different clinical associations: tumor-proximal neutrophils are linked to favorable prognosis, whereas neutrophils near immune cells associate with immunotherapy response.

title: The future of early endpoints for neoadjuvant therapy
abstract: Early endpoints as surrogates for long-term outcomes are essential for treatment efficacy evaluation. In this issue of Cancer Cell, Conforti et al. report that CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore scores predict long-term outcomes at the patient level but not at the trial level, highlighting the need for better early endpoints that reliably capture efficacy across trials.

title: Targeting F. nucleatum with metronidazole plus tislelizumab and fruquintinib in MSS colorectal cancer: A multicenter phase 2 study
abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum has been linked to chemoresistance and immune evasion in colorectal cancer (CRC), but therapeutic strategies targeting this bacterium remain limited. In this multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 trial (NCT06356597), 33 patients with Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive, microsatellite-stable metastatic CRC received the combination treatment of tislelizumab, fruquintinib, and the antimicrobial metronidazole. The primary endpoint was met, with a median progression-free survival of 6.0 months. The objective response rate and disease control rate were 19.4% and 83.9%, respectively. Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 30.3% of patients, with no grade 4 or 5 events. Metagenomic analysis showed that metronidazole reduced Fusobacterium nucleatum abundance. Exploratory analyses associated clinical benefit with enrichment of Lactobacillus species and nonresponse with Enterococcus. Fecal microbiota transplantation from responders sensitized germ-free mice to the treatment, which enhanced cytotoxic CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell differentiation and reduced terminal exhaustion. These findings support further evaluation of this combination in Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive metastatic CRC.

title: Antibiotics counteracting tumor-promoting dysbiosis in colorectal cancer
abstract: Antibiotics usually sabotage immune checkpoint blockade. In this issue of Cancer Cell, Jiang et al. report that pulsed, anaerobe-directed metronidazole added to an anti-PD-1 antibody and a VEGF receptor inhibitor achieved encouraging progression-free survival in Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive microsatellite-stable metastatic colorectal cancer, selectively dismantling a pathobiont network without inducing global dysbiosis.
